signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Divergence
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5741 as the Australian Dollar emerges as the G10 leader with a +0.809% weekly average gain, while the Swiss Franc lags at -0.335%. The 1.144% spread reflects a powerful bilateral theme driven by a massive +435bp carry advantage for the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.00%). Geopolitical headlines involving the Strait of Hormuz and potential energy supply shifts are currently being absorbed in a mixed-regime environment, with VIX at 15.5 favoring carry persistence over safe-haven demand. This divergence is reinforced by a restrictive +0.55% AUD real rate compared to a -0.40% accommodative CHF real rate. Technically, AUD/USD remains constructive while holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry advantage dominates while VIX remains below 25. Catalyst: Australian Inflation data 26 August. Risk: A sudden spike in VIX above 25 triggers a rapid safe-haven bid in CHF, compressing the carry spread.

signals.title: EUR/USD — ECB Hawkish Repricing + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD at 1.1681 is buoyed by TIER-1 headlines indicating ECB holds at 2.4%. This hawkish shift contrasts with the Fed's 3.75% hold stance, though a +135bp carry advantage still favors the USD. The options market is pricing in significant tail risk, with EUR/USD IV at 7.1% vs HV30 of 4.5%, creating a +2.6% vol risk premium. Speculative positioning remains heavily net short (LF net -76,035, pctl 10), suggesting an asymmetric squeeze risk if the ECB delivers a hawkish surprise. Price is currently positioned above the SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1561, 1.1479, and 1.1635 respectively. Trade bias: Bullish EUR/USD, driven by policy divergence and short-covering potential. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — Hike bias. Risk: US data outperformance strengthens the Fed's hold-for-longer narrative, supporting the USD carry lead.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Crowding vs Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.16 remains supported by a +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%), though the pair is trading just below its SMA20 of 159.19. The options market displays a strong put skew with 25d RR at -1.86, signalling that institutional desks are paying a premium for downside protection despite the carry-positive backdrop. This complacency in IV (7.2%) relative to realized vol (8.7%) results in a -1.5% VRP, which often precedes sharp moves when catalysts emerge. While COT JPY net shorts are not at 52-week extremes (pctl 38), the proximity to the 160.00 psychological level introduces verbal intervention risk from Japanese authorities. Trade bias: Neutral/Range USD/JPY; carry is offset by intervention fears near 160.00. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — Hike bias. Risk: A break above 160.00 triggers MoF/BoJ intervention, forcing a rapid liquidation of carry positions.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing 0.7170, maintaining a constructive stance above its SMA200 at 0.6957. Speculative positioning is leaning long with LF net +49,749 (pctl 81), but the move is meeting significant resistance from retail traders, where 89% are now short. This institutional vs retail divergence suggests a potential for further upside as retail stops are hunted in a trend continuation. Despite a moderate negative ESI of -8.5, the +60bp carry advantage for the AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%) continues to attract buyers in a sub-20 VIX environment. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail extreme short positioning suggests further trend extension. Catalyst: Australian Inflation data 26 August. Risk: A significant miss in CPI data leads to a dovish repricing of the RBA, invalidating the carry-led bid.
